comment: The vectors pinning Prima.ConsentPreview: every side reads the preview, which holds a row of every kind, and writes it back to the same map; accepts each origin spelling and refuses each invalid one; and refuses each refusal with the named reason. A preview carries no sentence. Only egress, storage, tools and limits can be narrowed. Origins are answered in the enum's order: interactive, programmatic, schedule, webhook. A row is one per kind and node; a credential one per binding, keyed by its binding_key: the row's node, the edge it rides (@ingress for the node's own key, otherwise the dependency's name-level ref, ref|need for a named need) and its slot (default, or name:<connection> for a named account); a stream one per name and subject; a tool server and a card one per name. So one entry lent on two edges is two rows, and so is one stream under two subjects. A credential row names the entry's provider hint (absent when it has none), its destination in Prima.Destination's canonical spelling, its source (own, instance or provided), whether it is disclosed, suggested and a choice the person must make, and its lifetime: standing, until an RFC 3339 UTC time, or once. A tools row names tool.action names, or * alone and never narrowed when the ask names every tool and the grant is the whole ask. A preview names the bindings of the profile's head the revision removes, as removed: a list, empty when it removes none, sorted by binding_key, each key once. Each removal is one binding as the head's row holds it: its binding_key, node, edge and connection (absent for a default) spelled as a credential row's, the need it was bound for (null when it cannot be told), exactly one of entry_id, instance_entry_id and via (the lender's label), and the entry's name and source (own or instance), each absent when the entry cannot be read.
